definition.availability_rule: Use only observed closes at or before signal close t. Current historical download is not a vintage archive.
definition.execution_rule: No earlier than next observed close after t; last-row signal has no execution observation. No tradability or performance claim.
definition.hypothesis: Model hypothesis appears separately below; it is not a computed result.
definition.input_units: Unadjusted close in CNY/share; simple returns and final score dimensionless.
definition.name: Trailing close-return research candidate
definition.signal_rule: Signal after close t; require 6 trailing observations, positive volatility when normalized. No extra return-magnitude eligibility exclusion.
definition.universe: 601318.XSHG, 600036.XSHG, 300750.XSHE; fixed convenience sample, not a point-in-time universe.

limits: Development sample only; this inspected data cannot become an untouched holdout.
An available next observed close does not establish tradability, fills or transaction costs.
Raw return and volatility-normalized return are both dimensionless; scaling changes magnitude, not units.
No forward labels, returns after execution, alpha, causality or superiority were measured.
Unadjusted historical closes are not vintage data or evidence of corporate actions.
The observed-date sample is neither an exchange calendar nor a representative market universe.

citations.quote: Descriptive score differences cannot establish superiority.
A coherent retention or inconclusive proposal is allowed.
All signal calculations use observations at/before t; execution no earlier than the next observed close.

decisions.reason: Adopted: no defect is recorded at the observed grain, so no return-magnitude eligibility bound is justified; the retained candidate adds no exclusion, matching the evidence.
Adopted: timing already conforms - scores use only closes observed at or before the signal close and execution is no earlier than the next observed close; no tradability is claimed.
Inspected the exact alternative: coverage kept, dispersion positive, yet cross-name score spread stays as wide with inverted ordering, so the comparability motive is unobserved; no change forced.
Adopted: descriptive summaries cannot show superiority, alpha or a winning direction; mixed-sign means and any scale change are observations only, and unproven alpha does not bar exploration.

hypothesis.text: Exploratory short-horizon close-momentum research candidate, retained unchanged: the trailing close return over the configured lookback, taken in the configured direction, with no volatility scaling and no return-magnitude eligibility bound. A signal is formed after an observed close using only closes at or before it; the earliest price observation for any later evaluation is the next observed close. Usefulness, sign and any investment benefit are unproven and reserved for a separate future evaluation; this is a research proposal, not deployment.

rationale.text: Retention follows from cited evidence, not inertia. The frozen panel is complete at the observed grain with no recorded defect, so no eligibility bound is justified and none is added. The single motivated alternative, volatility scaling at the same lookback and direction, was inspected on its exact spec: it preserves required closes per signal, warmup exclusions, eligible signals and next-close availability with positive dispersion in every window, yet the hypothesized gain in cross-name comparability is not observed, because score dispersion across the names remains about as wide, its ordering inverts, and the sign pattern of mean scores changes under scaling. With no forward labels, execution returns, costs or corporate-action information, that observed score-scale difference cannot establish improvement, superiority, a winning direction, removed systematic risk or executable trades, so the added parameter is unsupported and the simpler raw spec is retained. The alternative remains a possible arm for a later labeled evaluation, together with vintage price data and defined execution assumptions.
